content:
@Michał Mrugała and I are running a project to formalise toric varieties, which are strongly combinatorial objects in algebraic geometry.

We are basing ourselves on the hefty book by Cox, Little and Schenck, with the current goal being the formalisation of Chapter 1.

The project has:

  • A GitHub repository
  • A website
  • A blueprint, currently covering sections 1.1 and 1.2 of Cox-Little-Schenck.
  • A dedicated stream on this Zulip: #toric
  • Several upstreamed contributions to Mathlib already
  • Multiple contributors, who we are grateful to: @Andrew Yang, @Patrick Luo, @Paul Lezeau

This is a call for contribution

We are looking for people interested in either scheme theory or convex analysis with arbitrary levels of Lean experience. At this stage of the project, there are plenty of easy items to grab, as well as hard ones to chew on.

If you are interested, feel free to contact us, or head over directly to #toric > Current tasks and claim a task!

The first phase of the Toric project is over! We now know that affine group schemes correspond to Hopf algebras, and have formalised a few more goodies too:

  • Diagonalisable group schemes
  • Tori
  • The character-cocharacter pairing
  • SO(2, k) as a group scheme

There is a new blogpost explaining all this, and more here.

All of this work is currently in Toric, and we look forward to your reviews on the relevant PRs: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/labels/toric :wink:

We are looking for collaborators. If any task in the blueprint speaks to you, then please head to #toric > Current tasks and claim it!
